Phil Scott

Republican candidate for Governor, Vermont · Incumbent

Governor of Vermont (incumbent)

Phil Scott is the Republican governor of Vermont. He lives in Berlin and was first elected in 2016. On May 28, 2026, he filed to run for a sixth two-year term, and he is the Republican nominee on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

Where Scott stands

Affordability and cost of living
Calls Vermont's affordability crisis one of his main concerns. Says he will keep pushing policies he believes will grow the economy and lower the cost of living.
Property taxes
Urged lawmakers in the 2026 session to use state revenue again to offset projected property tax increases.
Education governance and funding
Proposes overhauling Vermont's education system by consolidating school districts and changing how schools are funded.
State workforce
Issued a return-to-office mandate for state employees and has kept it in place despite a dispute with the state employees union.
Relationship with national Republican Party
Says he differs with President Trump on many issues and has shown he is independent of the party.

Background

  • Governor of Vermont, 2017–present (first elected 2016; re-elected 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024)
  • Won the 2024 general election with 73% of the vote
  • Filed for re-election to a sixth term on May 28, 2026
  • Resides in Berlin, Vermont
